title: Mum's Oldest — EN/ES/FR (Wilma McIvor)
style: folk country acoustic guitar warm female vocal 98bpm brushed drums gentle storytelling English Spanish French language learning trilingual
lyrics:
[Verse 1 — English]
He came first, and that changes a person
You carry the weight of the ones who come after
I watched him on rooftops and I held my breath
But he was sure-footed, always was

[Verse 2 — Español]
Cuando llamó para decir que compraba el bote [When he rang to say he was buying the boat]
Preparé una taza de té y me senté por un rato [I made a cup of tea and sat for a while]
Tu padre se rió — claro que sí, claro que sí [Your father laughed — of course he did, of course]
Ese es el niño que nunca se quedó quieto para mí [That's the boy who never stayed still for me]

[Chorus — English]
My oldest one, the one who led the way
My oldest one, I see him in the early day
Standing at the water, looking for the line
My oldest one — I'm glad you're doing fine

[Bridge — Français]
Mon fils aîné regarde l'horizon [My oldest son looks at the horizon]
Il a toujours su où il devait aller [He always knew where he needed to go]
Le jardin pousse encore, la vie continue [The garden is still growing, life goes on]
Mon fils aîné — je suis si fière de toi [My oldest son — I am so proud of you]

[Verse 3 — English]
He runs his boats and I run my garden
Different kinds of captain, same steady hands

[Outro — EN/ES/FR]
The gardens still growing
El jardín sigue creciendo [The garden is still growing]
Le jardin pousse encore [The garden is still growing]
My oldest one
